To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expanded ECM is a valid model for predicting continued IT usage behavior, and it can provide useful information to IT product/service providers.

the expanded expectation-confirmation model, incorporating post-adoption perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use (PEOU) and perceived enjoyment (PEN), can provide a better understanding of the continued usage of mobile Internet services than the traditional expectation-confirmation model.

(1) The expanded ECM has good predictive power in explaining the continued usage intention and satisfaction of mobile Internet users, and (2) The significant effects of perceived ease of use (pEOU) and perceived enjoyment (pENJ) on the expanded ECM indicate that the nature of IT is an important boundary condition to consider in the application of the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model of IT adoption that is based on the ECM.
the development of an expanded ECM that incorporates post-adoption beliefs into the ECM.
the effects of post-adop-tion beliefs on the ECM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expanded ECM, incorporating perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use of the IT, and perceived enjoyment of the IT, has good explanatory power, with all paths supported, in understanding continued IT usage behavior, with perceived ease of use as a boundary condition.

the ECM is a useful and valid model for understanding the determinants of continued IT usage behavior, and that it is capable of providing additional insights into the determinants of satisfaction and continued IT usage behavior when it is expanded to incorporate post-adoption beliefs.

, the results of this study show that the expanded ECM, incorporating post-adoption beliefs, has a good explanatory power (r 2 = 0.576 for continued usage intention, and r 2 =  0.678 for satisfaction) in the context of mobile Internet services, with all paths supported in the structural equation modeling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study provides a more holistic understanding of the continued usage intention of information technology, which can be used to guide future research and practice.
we have successfully extended the ECM by including post-adoption beliefs.
the study of post-adoption belief is a promising research avenue for understanding continued information technology (hereafter referred to as IT) usage behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IT product/service providers should not only focus on the instrumental value of their products/services, but also on the affective and hedonic values of their products/services.

the ECM can be expanded to incorporate post-adoption beliefs, which are relevant to the understanding of continued IT usage behavior, and the expanded ECM can be applied to IT products/services beyond an instrumental focus.
the expanded ECM is a more robust model than the ECM, in terms of its explanatory power and the ability to identify the determinants of continued IT usage.
